title: Quantifiers: much, many, a lot of, a few, a little, too, enough
en:
Countable (people, reports, days): many, a few, how many. Uncountable (time, money, information, work): much, a little, how much. Both: a lot of / lots of.

In positive sentences we usually say a lot of; much / many are more common in negatives and questions: We don't have much time. Are there many people?

too + adjective / too much / too many + noun = more than is good: It's too expensive. I have too much work.

not + adjective + enough; enough + noun: The room isn't big enough. We don't have enough chairs.
ru: Исчисляемые (reports, people) — many, a few, how many; неисчисляемые (time, money, information, work) — much, a little, how much. a lot of — с обоими. too — слишком; too much / too many + сущ. enough: прилагательное + enough, но enough + существительное.

boss.situation: Describe your workload this month: too much / too many / not enough / a lot of / a few.
samples: This month I have too much work.
There are too many reports to check.
We don't have enough people in the team.
I only have a few free hours a week.
The deadline is too close and the time is not enough.

qs.exp: time uncountable, small amount → a little.

qs.q: I know ___ people in the Astana office.
qs.exp: people countable, small number → a few.

qs.q: This coffee is ___ hot. I can't drink it.
“Information” is uncountable, so we say “much information”.
“We don't have chairs enough” is correct.
qs.exp: enough goes before a noun: enough chairs.
